author_or_org: Om Nepal, Sushant Aryal, Oluseyi Olukola, Nick Rahimi

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The paper argues that compile rate is a scientifically unreliable metric for single-function vulnerability repair, based on five controlled experiments over 203 vulnerable functions, three open-source code LLMs ranging from 350M to 6.7B parameters, and three prompting strategies.
claims.quote: We argue that compile rate is a scientifically unreliable metric for single-function vulnerability repair, and we support this with five controlled experiments over 203 vulnerable functions from Big-Vul, three open-source code LLMs (350M to 6.7B parameters), and three prompting strategies.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: About 64% of compile failures are not attributable to the model and that share is nearly invariant across models, with compile rate dominated by evaluation-harness and dataset artifacts rather than model quality.
claims.quote: Compile rate (i) barely responds to an intervention that substantially improves the generated code; (ii) is dominated by evaluation-harness and dataset artifacts rather than model quality, with about 64% of compile failures not attributable to the model, a share that is nearly invariant across models;

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: When used as an optimization target, compile rate rewards non-repairs: a compiler-feedback loop raises compile rate while similarity to the human fix falls, and manual inspection finds deletion- and placeholder-style non-repairs among newly compiling outputs.
claims.quote: (v) rewards non-repairs when used as an optimization target, since a compiler-feedback loop raises compile rate while similarity to the human fix falls, with manual inspection finding deletion- and placeholder-style non-repairs among the newly compiling outputs.

claims.claim: The whole-function CodeBLEU fallback also fails because an unchanged copy of the vulnerable input outscores every model.
claims.quote: The natural fallback, whole-function CodeBLEU, also fails: an unchanged copy of the vulnerable input outscores every model.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: diff_F1, a change-aware screen that scores only the edited region, gives exactly zero credit to a no-op and near-zero credit to some deletion-based gaming patches while still crediting genuine partial edits, but it is not a repair-quality metric.
claims.quote: We also examine diff_F1, a change-aware screen that scores only the edited region. It gives exactly zero credit to a no-op and near-zero credit to some, though not all, of the deletion-based gaming patches we observed, while still crediting genuine partial edits, so it may serve as a cheap screen before deeper, execution-based analysis. It is not a repair-quality metric, and we report where it falls short.
